raw_cue_correspondence.text: Certifications brings together the types your department tracks and
the records held by people or units.
In this fictional Chicago Fire department, the dashboard starts
with one record pending verification.
Boden can inspect his own pending record, but this page offers no Verify button.
Record holders cannot verify their own records.
We will create a clearly marked software exercise for another member, then use
the normal administrative review path.
Use the viewing, management, and setup permissions your department has assigned.
Choose Certification types.
The table separates each stable code, category, scope, validity,
record count, and requirement count.
Template gallery opens a separate selection window.
Enter SAR in its filter to inspect relevant starter entries.
Their displayed names, authorities, and validity periods are catalog starting
points that your department must review.
Keep every checkbox clear and use Cancel; nothing is added.
We will create our own fictional Person type so the software exercise
is distinct from the existing types.
Choose New type.
Enter Training Only, Record Review, followed by the
exercise date, as the Type.
Give it the explicit code TRN-REVIEW-20261028.
A stable, recognizable code helps distinguish this type
later in tables and integrations.
Keep Category as Other and Applies to as Person.
Enter Academy Software Exercise, marked fictional, as the Issuing authority.
The Description explicitly identifies a software verification exercise and
says that it is not a professional qualification or authorization.
Set Default validity to twelve months and leave Never expires clear.
Credit hours per renewal stays blank.
Check Requires supervisor verification and keep Active checked.
The help explains that new records remain pending until someone with
required_labels: New records stay pending until someone with manage rights signs them off.

raw_cue_correspondence.text: management rights signs them off.
Use Save, then read the returned catalog row.
Our code is present, its scope is Person, and its validity is twelve months.
Both Records and Requirements are zero: creating this type
has not created a member record or attached a role requirement.
On the dashboard, choose Add Certification.
This administrative form has an explicit Member selector.
Choose Matthew Casey, then select the new training type.
Check the selected member and type together before entering
identifying information.
Notice that Issued on and Expires on are still blank after selecting the type.
The type’s twelve-month setting has not filled these fields on this form.
We will enter the intended exercise dates explicitly rather than
assume that a date was calculated.
Use Training Only, Software Record Review as the Name and the
DEMO-CASEY-REVIEW number shown here.
Valid Area says Academy training department only, and Issued by
repeats our fictional software issuer.
Enter October twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-six as the issue
date and October twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-seven as the expiry.
File is optional and remains empty.
Save once.
The returned dashboard reports Saved and now has two pending records.
Saving the record did not automatically complete its required verification.
Here is Casey’s saved record.
Read its member, type, number, and expiry before using Verify.
This button submits the review directly.
The returned record is Active and shows Verified by Wallace
Boden with the displayed date.
Open the record again and check that the same status and reviewer remain.
This confirms the stored software review.
It does not establish that a real qualification was earned.
We leave renewal, credits, suspension, and revocation
unchanged throughout this exercise.
Use Matthew Casey’s member link to open his holdings.
The table lists each record separately with its name, type, expiry, and status.
The existing Firefighter qualification remains, and the new training
review appears on another row with its own date and Active status.
Compare the exact record name and type before opening or editing anything.
This person view helps you distinguish a newly added exercise record from an
older record that should remain untouched.
Return through Certification types.
Our row now has one Record and still has zero Requirements.
Use that row’s Edit control to inspect the saved type.
Applies to is disabled at Person because a record now references it.
Code remains editable here; code locking applies when role
requirements reference the type.
The lower options still show twelve months, verification
required, and Active checked.
This is a readback only.
We do not change the code, add a role requirement, or save another type update.
Settings separates role enforcement from expiry notifications.
The saved mode is Off, with thirty days of grace and pending records not
required_labels: Treat records pending verification as valid for role requirements

raw_cue_correspondence.text: treated as valid for role requirements.
Warn only permits role changes with warnings; Enforce can block
unqualified role additions and remove members after grace.
We inspect these choices, restore Off, and leave Save untouched.
Off does not disable expiry processing or notifications.
The holder and administrator-digest options remain checked, with lead days of
required_labels: Send department administrators a nightly digest

raw_cue_correspondence.text: sixty, thirty, fourteen, seven, and one.

raw_cue_correspondence.text: These settings do not prove message delivery.
On the dashboard, Group is filtered to Truck 81.
Five member rows appear, including Casey’s new expiry under the training code.
The Pending verification card still describes the department,
not just these filtered rows.
Export CSV is available for the current filters; no file is downloaded here.
Choose Compliance report to open the HTML report.
In Casey’s row, the training column shows the same expiry and Active status.
Read that actual row rather than infer a status from a color or a total.
Chicago Fire can use this pattern to organize a clearly
identified exercise record.
Community care and mental health teams can track operational
training without patient detail.
Search and rescue can distinguish person records from equipment records;
security teams can organize reviewed staff records; wildland teams can keep
seasonal training references current; and industrial response teams can separate
staff records from unit inspections.
In every setting, define the type, enter deliberate dates, use an authorized
reviewer, and verify saved status.
A software label alone does not authorize real duties.
